question: Boron is the only metalloid of which group of the periodic table?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Group 13**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Boron** is the only metalloid in **Group 13** of the periodic table.
 
• Group 13 elements are also known as the **boron group**, which includes boron (B), aluminum (Al), gallium (Ga), indium (In), and thallium (Tl).
 
• Among these elements, **boron** exhibits properties of both metals and non-metals, classifying it as a metalloid.
 
• Metalloids have intermediate properties and are often semiconductors, which boron also exhibits.
 
• Boron is essential for plant growth and has various industrial applications, including in borosilicate glass and detergents.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Group 13** elements typically have three electrons in their outermost shell, leading to a +3 oxidation state in compounds.
 
• Boron compounds, such as borates, are used in glassmaking, ceramics, and as a mild antiseptic.
 
• Boron is also a component of boron nitride, a material with properties similar to carbon-based materials like graphite and diamond.
 
• In the periodic table, boron is located in period 2, making it the lightest element in Group 13.
 
• The unique properties of boron, such as its high melting point and hardness, make it useful in various high-temperature and abrasive environments.
